what: The system cursor is hidden and a 50px circle that inverts 30% of what is beneath it and blurs it by 10px follows the mouse with no lag. Over a clickable target it shrinks to .5x, and while pressed to .9x, riding a spring (size tension 150.93 · friction 19.56 clamp, press 129.69 · 8.24, so the press wobbles slightly). Within 10px of the window edge the circle slides out past the nearest edge in .15s, and slides back in from that side when it returns. The feel of a cursor lighting up what is beneath it like a lens on a white portfolio

options.target: CSS target to shrink, default a, button, [data-clickable]
options.edge: Distance at which it starts slipping off the window edge (px), default 10
options.slide: Seconds to go out past the edge and come back in, default .15 — 0 means immediate
options.native: with show, the system cursor is not hidden
options.[data-fx-part=lens]: Circle (optional) — if missing, the part creates one

note: The springs use the same integration as react-spring v9 (1ms step, mass 1), so entering the original values gives the same bounce. On touch devices (no hover) nothing is attached. Durations are rough values for how long the spring takes to settle

from.where: index.html .mm-cursor-wrap — original cursor_cursor (50px · backdrop invert(30%) blur(10px)) · constants table cursorScaleSmall .5 · cursorScaleDown .9 · cursorScaleSpring 150.93265/19.56007 clamp · cursorDownSpring 129.69176/8.24223 · data-clickable targets · at 10px from the window edge (EdgeDistance) it moves out past the nearest edge by its radius (speed measured with motion-probe over 150ms).
